intent: Make a chat turn always reach a terminal state. Source: the operator's second live Hermes QA pass, 2026-08-29, finding A9, which saw assistant rows with status failed and error null, and one stuck at streaming showing 'No response', and guessed the cause was environmental. Half right: the trigger is usually a gateway that returned nothing, but the reason it looks like a silent failure and never heals is app code in three places. useChatSend finalised fast mode without the error it had just displayed; reconcilePendingChatMessages heals a turn by looking up its run and fast mode never has one, so a tab closed mid-stream left a row streaming for the life of the database; and undefined means leave-unchanged in the reconciler, so a failed run carrying no error left the column as it was. Closed 2026-08-29.
invariants: I1 A turn that cannot be healed is eventually failed, with a reason. failStuckChatMessages sweeps rows with no run behind them and rows whose run has been pruned away.

I2 A turn that CAN be healed is left alone. A row whose run still exists belongs to the reconciler however old it is, because sweeping it would race a live agent turn that is simply taking its time. Asserted explicitly, and the mutation that removes the exemption turns it red.
I3 The sweep respects an age cutoff. Without it the sweep would fail live streams; the mutation that removes the cutoff turns all eleven red.
I4 A displayed reason is a saved reason. Fast mode persists the error it shows, as agent mode always has.
I5 A failure always says something, a success clears what a previous attempt left behind.
oracle_provenance: Authored BEFORE any production file was opened for edit and committed on its own at 1b943f07, ahead of the implementation at 1ac31b49. One file, tests/unit/chat-does-not-wedge.test.ts, measured against dev@4861bd68: 11 red of 11. The oracle commit message says '11 failed, 1 passed' and is WRONG: a new function cannot be behaviourally red before it exists, so every assertion in the file failed on the missing export. Recorded here rather than amended, as with T-0049.
verification: Five mutations against the committed implementation, tree restored and confirmed clean after each: stopping the sweep turns 4 red; removing the age cutoff turns all 11 red; removing the run-still-exists exemption turns 1 red; narrowing the sweep back to run_id IS NULL turns 1 red (the pruned-run case); dropping the reason turns 2 red.
harness_defect_found: Worth recording because it cost real time and will cost the next person the same. better-sqlite3 is mapped to a stub in jest.config.js, so `new Database(':memory:')` inside a test yields a no-op driver that swallows every write and returns nothing. The first version of this oracle asserted against an empty database and reported `rows in db: []` with no error anywhere, which reads exactly like a product bug. Every repository test in this repo reaches past the mapper with jest.requireActual for the real driver; this one now does too, and the file says why in a comment so the next author does not spend the same hour.
scope_beyond_the_report: The report asked what happens when the SSE drops client-side. The answer turned out to have two shapes, not one. The fast-mode wedge is the one it saw. The other is a turn whose RUN has since been pruned: the reconciler looks the run up, finds nothing, and moves on forever. Same permanent wedge, different route, and it is covered here.
rollback: Revert 1ac31b49. The oracle at 1b943f07 then goes red again. No schema change involved.
deferred: The sweep runs at boot only, like the Deep Research one it mirrors. A long-lived server that never restarts will hold a wedged row until it does. Putting it on the BackgroundScheduler tick is the obvious next step and is deliberately not done here: the research sweep has the same shape, and changing one without the other would leave two recovery paths that disagree. Worth one record covering both.

The PATCH route at chat/[id]/messages/[messageId] still treats a non-string error as leave-unchanged. The reconciler no longer relies on that, and the client now always sends a string on failure, so nothing reaches it with the old shape today. Left alone rather than changed speculatively.
